description: Challenge B2 content batch for The Sound Maze. Each target is spoken aloud; the learner selects its spelling. Draft content is not wired into the live game.

questions.explain: Frivolous has /ɪ/ in its first stressed syllable. Fabulous has /æ/, fervent has /ɜr/, and frenzy has /ɛ/.
Quandary has /ɑ/ in its first syllable in General American. The other forms are not standard spellings.
Laconic has /ə/ in the first unstressed syllable and /ɑ/ in the stressed second syllable. Laconicity has a different stress pattern; the other forms are not standard spellings.
Pterodactyl begins with /t/ because the initial p is silent. Tether also begins with /t/ but has a different vowel and ending; theory begins with /θ/ and deter with /d/.
Phlegm begins with /f/, written ph. Flame has /eɪ/, them begins with /ð/, and realm begins with /r/.
Gnostic begins with /n/ because the initial g is silent. Magnetic begins with /m/, genetic with /dʒ/, and kinetic with /k/.
Lengths ends with /ŋθs/ in careful General American pronunciation. Length ends with /ŋθ/, lenses with /ɪz/, and lengthen with /ən/.
Sixths ends with the cluster /ksθs/. Sixes ends with /ɪz/, sixth with /θ/, and sickles with /əlz/.
Glimpsed ends with /pst/: -ed is pronounced /t/ after the voiceless /s/ sound. Glimpse ends with /ps/, glimpses with /ɪz/, and glimmer with /ər/.
Yacht is pronounced /jɑt/; the ch is silent and the spelling is unusual. Yolk ends with /k/, yawn with /n/, and yak with /k/ after a different vowel.
Fuchsia is pronounced /ˈfjuːʃə/. Future has /tʃər/, fusion has /ʒən/, and fugue ends with /ɡ/.
Connoisseur is pronounced /ˌkɑnəˈsɜr/. Conqueror, conductor, and conservator have different stressed syllables and endings.
